newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH sees lower 1997 DFS results.
newsitem.headline: LVMH sees lower 1997 DFS results.

text.p: LVMH Chairman Bernard Arnault said on Thursday the company's newly acquired Duty Free Shoppers (DFS) unit would show lower results in 1997.
"DFS is performing slightly less well this year," Arnault told the annual general meeting of Christian Dior SA, one of the holding companies of LVMH.
"Its results should be slightly inferior to those of last year due in part to the weakness of the yen," he said.
LVMH said in March when it reported its 1996 results that its objective was to show a rise in results and turnover in 1997 excluding the impact of the acquisition of Duty Free Shoppers.

Its 1996 profit fell to 3.68 billion francs from 4.05 billion in 1995 after it reported a capital loss on the sale of a third of its stake in Guinness Plc to help pay for the $2.6 billion acquisition of San Francisco-based DFS.

Arnault said the yen's weakness had been unfavourable for DFS's Japanese clients. Coupled with DFS's investment plans, "the two elements risk weighing momentarily on the profitability of DFS's activities.
Nonetheless, DFS's contribution to LVMH's net pre-exceptional result will be positive in 1997," he said.
LVMH said in January that the DFS acquisition would have a positive impact on cashflow and pre-exceptional profit before goodwill amortisation but weigh on earnings per share.
